Choose the model with the best test score
Deploy the model to users

choices.text: Fit the scaler on all rows, then split
Fit the scaler on training rows; apply that fitted scaler to test rows

A category name such as red, blue, or green
A measured temperature in degrees Celsius

questions.prompt: For the fitted line y_hat = 0.09 + 1.99 x, what does the slope 1.99 mean in this example?

choices.text: The prediction rises by 1.99 for a one-unit increase in x, within the modeled range
The prediction at x = 0 is 1.99
Every observed y value is exactly 1.99
The model has 1.99 features

questions.explanation: The slope is the fitted change in the prediction for a one-unit increase in the input, within the modeled range.

questions.prompt: For the fitted line y_hat = 0.09 + 1.99 x, what does the model predict when x = 6?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 6: 0.09 + 1.99 times 6 = 12.03.

questions.prompt: A residual-versus-fitted plot shows residuals mostly negative at low fitted values, positive in the middle, and negative again at high fitted values. Residual means observed minus predicted. What is the best next interpretation?

choices.text: The U-shaped pattern suggests the straight-line model misses a systematic curve; investigate a suitable feature form
The line proves that x causes y
Negative residuals mean the model predicted too low
The residual plot proves the data contain no measurement error

questions.explanation: A curved pattern is a diagnostic signal to investigate model form and data. It does not prove causation or identify the cause by itself. Negative observed-minus-predicted residuals mean predictions were too high on those rows.

questions.prompt: For one row, the observed value is 9 and the prediction is 11. Using residual = observed minus predicted, what is the residual and what does it mean?

choices.text: -2; the prediction is two units too high
+2; the prediction is two units too low
20; the prediction is exact
-2; the prediction is two units too low

questions.explanation: 9 - 11 = -2. A negative residual means the model predicted above the observed value.

questions.prompt: One word only: name a visible residual pattern that could prompt an investigation (for example, curve). Do not enter personal information.
questions.explanation: A curve, funnel, cluster, or other structure can be worth investigating; a plot is diagnostic evidence, not proof of cause.

questions.prompt: A linear regression uses both temperature and humidity as inputs to predict demand. What makes it multiple regression?

choices.text: It has more than one target
It uses more than one predictor feature

It cannot be fit with least squares

questions.prompt: For one input x = 3 and degree 2, what row does PolynomialFeatures(include_bias=True) produce?
questions.explanation: For one input and degree 2, the basis is [1, x, x squared], so x = 3 maps to [1, 3, 9].

questions.prompt: Why can a polynomial regression curve still be called linear in its parameters?

choices.text: The input x is never transformed
The model is a straight line for every value of x
The expanded features are combined linearly using fitted coefficients
A polynomial model has no coefficients

questions.explanation: A feature map such as [1, x, x squared] can make predictions curve with x while the coefficients enter as a linear weighted sum.

Replace the training set with the test set
Guarantee zero prediction error
Turn every regression target into a class label

questions.explanation: 0.63 is greater than 0.50, so the decision rule prints class 1. This is not a claim of certainty.

questions.prompt: In a confusion matrix with rows = true labels and columns = predicted labels, where is a false negative for positive class 1?

choices.text: True row 1, predicted column 0
True row 0, predicted column 1
True row 1, predicted column 1

questions.explanation: A false negative is a real positive example that was predicted as negative. State the row/column convention when presenting a matrix.

questions.task: Choose a metric for a rare positive class
questions.prompt: A rare positive class matters, and missing a real positive case is more costly than investigating a false alarm. Which metric should the team prioritize first while reviewing the threshold?

choices.text: Accuracy, because it counts all rows equally
Recall, because it measures the fraction of real positives found
Precision, because it measures the fraction of predicted negatives that are correct
R-squared, because every classifier is a regression model

questions.explanation: Recall = TP/(TP+FN). Precision = TP/(TP+FP). Prioritize using the stated costs; precision and recall trade off as the threshold changes.

questions.prompt: One word only: name a concept used to turn a predicted probability into a class label. Do not enter personal information.
questions.explanation: A threshold or cutoff is used to turn an estimated probability into a class decision.
